identity.name: Tragacanth gum
identity.chemical_class: Natural exudate acidic polysaccharide hydrocolloid (plant gum) from Astragalus species

function.mechanism: Hydrocolloid that increases viscosity and stabilizes emulsions/suspensions; EFSA reports it is unlikely to be absorbed intact and is partially fermented by intestinal microbiota.

adi.basis: EFSA (2017) concluded there is no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern for the general population at refined exposure and reported use levels.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation reported no genotoxicity concern, no adverse effects in carcinogenicity studies at highest tested doses, and no need for a numerical ADI for E413.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA database lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED for tragacanth gum (INS 413).

concerns.summary: Historical case reports and letters describe hypersensitivity/allergic reactions in some individuals where tragacanth was implicated; immunogenicity studies of exudate gums also support plausibility of sensitization in susceptible people.
EFSA notes partial fermentation by intestinal microbiota; available evidence in the EFSA re-evaluation did not identify this as a general-population safety concern at refined exposures.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2017: no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern for general population at refined exposure
EFSA 2017: no concern with respect to genotoxicity
Human volunteer study (1984): 9.9 g/day for 21 days was well tolerated without adverse toxicological findings
Rat ultrastructural study (1984): no detectable heart/liver pathological abnormalities at tested dietary levels

adi_exceedance.notes: ADI exceedance assessment is not directly applicable because EFSA concluded no numerical ADI is needed and JECFA ADI is not specified.

risk_assessment.rationale: E413 is broadly accepted by major regulators (EU approved, US CFR Part 184 GRAS framework, JECFA ADI not specified) with no convincing evidence of broad-population toxicological harm at authorized uses. However, historical hypersensitivity evidence indicates non-zero risk in susceptible individuals, preventing a risk_free designation.
key_factors: EFSA 2017 concluded no numerical ADI needed and no general-population safety concern
JECFA lists ADI as not specified with last toxicological evaluation year 1985
US eCFR lists gum tragacanth under 21 CFR 184.1351 within Part 184 GRAS framework with use limits
No IARC carcinogenic classification entry identified
Historical case reports indicate rare allergy/hypersensitivity potential
